citeAs: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, et al. (2025). Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. OpenThoughts Team.
creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, and others (OpenThoughts Team, Stanford University, BespokeLabs.ai, Toyota Research Institute, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, UCLA, JSC, LAION, NYU, UNC Chapel Hill)
description: A 1,000-example sample subset drawn from the OpenThoughts reasoning SFT dataset series. The OpenThoughts datasets consist of question–thinking-tokens–answer triplets across math, code, and science domains, where reasoning traces are distilled from teacher models (e.g., DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B). This sample is used for scaling experiments and ablations in the OpenThoughts project.
name: OpenThoughts-1k-sample
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reasoning traces (answers) were generated by querying teacher LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B, or Phi-4-Reasoning-Plus) on each question. For OpenThoughts-114K, answer matching and unit tests were used to verify math and code responses, filtering out incorrect answers. For OpenThoughts3, no answer filtering was applied as it did not improve performance. Multiple answers (up to 16×) were sampled per question using temperature=0.7, top_p=1.0, max_new_tokens=32768.
rai:dataBiases: Question sources are limited to a small number of high-quality sources (top 1-2 per domain), which may reduce diversity. The dataset is dominated by math (850K), code (250K), and science (100K) in OpenThoughts3, reflecting a deliberate domain imbalance. Decontamination was performed to remove evaluation benchmark overlap, but 1.4% of non-contaminated samples may be incorrectly removed. The use of LLM teachers (QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1) may introduce biases from those models into the reasoning traces.
rai:dataCollection: Questions were sourced from existing datasets and newly generated sources across math, code, and science domains. For math, sources include OpenMath-2-Math and NuminaMath-1.5. For code, sources include StackExchange CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning. For science, sources include StackExchange Physics and Organic Chemistry PDFs. Answers (reasoning traces) were generated by querying teacher models (primarily DeepSeek-R1 or QwQ-32B) on the collected questions, producing question–thinking-tokens–answer triplets for SFT.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data includes questions from StackExchange forums (CodeGolf, Physics, Biology), competitive programming datasets (OpenCodeReasoning, CodeContests, TACO, Apps), math competition and textbook datasets (NuminaMath-1.5, OpenMath-2-Math, MathPile, AutoMathText), and science sources including organic chemistry PDFs and physics StackExchange. Reasoning traces were generated by teacher models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B) rather than sourced from humans.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset focuses only on SFT data and does not cover reinforcement learning datasets. The pipeline does not explore staged SFT or curriculum learning. Safety alignment is degraded when models are trained on this data. The dataset covers only math, code, and science domains. Distilled reasoning models trained on this data still show generalization deficits (strong performance fluctuations on reasoning-invariant problem variations). Some benchmarks (AMC23, MATH500) saturate at the largest scale, and others (HLE) do not respond to scale.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Multiple answers per question were sampled from teacher models (up to 16× per question) to increase dataset scale. Questions were randomly sampled to reach target dataset sizes. Domain mixing ratios were set (e.g., 850K math, 250K code, 100K science for OpenThoughts3-1.2M). For scaling experiments, subsets of 1K, 3K, 10K, 31.6K, 100K, 300K, and 1M examples were created from the full dataset.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Pipeline includes: (1) question filtering using LLM-based difficulty scoring (GPT-4o-mini) or response-length filtering (GPT-4.1-mini/nano); (2) deduplication using exact match or fuzzy deduplication based on Normalized Indel similarity (LCS metric); (3) decontamination against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram similarity (N=13, Qwen2-7B-Instruct tokenizer); (4) removal of proof-based questions where applicable; (5) filtering non-English answers and long-paragraph answers in some configurations.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables open-source development of reasoning models, democratizing access to training data previously only available to proprietary systems. However, safety analysis shows that SFT on reasoning data inadvertently degrades pre-existing safety alignment: OpenThinker3-7B trained on this data achieved a harmfulness rate of 55.5% on Harmbench (vs. 14.5% for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), indicating a clear trade-off between reasoning capability and safety. The dataset was released without explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data.
rai:dataUseCases: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of language models to develop reasoning capabilities in math, code, and science domains. Intended for training reasoning models that can produce long chains of thought (thinking tokens) to solve challenging problems. Also used for ablation studies and scaling experiments to understand data curation strategies for reasoning models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: DeepSeek-R1 (primary teacher model for earlier versions), QwQ-32B (primary teacher model for OpenThoughts3), GPT-4o-mini (used for question difficulty scoring, question generation from seed text, answer verification, and filtering), GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1-nano (used for response-length-based question filtering), FastText classifiers (used for question and answer filtering), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (used for embedding-based question filtering), Gemini gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (used for OCR of organic chemistry PDFs), Math-Verify toolkit (used for math answer extraction/verification).

null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are generated by LLM teacher models (not human annotators), so human annotator demographics are not applicable.
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The number of annotations per item varies by pipeline stage; up to 16 answers per question were generated but the final dataset uses a variable number depending on domain and deduplication strategy.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No crowdsourcing platform used; annotations generated via LLM API calls (DeepSeek API, OpenAI API).
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement analysis; annotations are LLM-generated, not human-annotated.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No explicit discussion of missing data handling in the dataset collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific data collection timeframe (start/end dates) is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values described; the pipeline generates or filters data rather than imputing.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan described beyond the series of releases (OpenThoughts 1, 2, 3).
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Dataset consists of math, code, and science reasoning problems with no personal or sensitive information collected.
